newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Business sees 11.8 pct rise in S.Africa Xmas sales.
newsitem.headline: Business sees 11.8 pct rise in S.Africa Xmas sales.

text.p: South Africa is set for a 11.8 percent rise in Christmas sales this year to 30 billion rand worth of goods despite a slowing down of the economy, a survey said on Tuesday.
The report, by the South African Chamber of Business (Sacob), said a price increase of 6.7 percent meant that the actual volume of goods sold in November and December would rise by 5.1 percent.
"Although consumers are still under constraints in terms of disposable income, the sales expectations of retailers for the 1996 Christmas period is good," Sacob said.
The Christmas months are vital to South African retailers, making up 22 percent of annual sales.

The picture in South Africa is, however, clouded by the fact that the period coincides with the country's main holiday season. "Christmas bonuses and savings have to fund vacation needs as well as gift purchases," Sacob said.
The movements of holiday-makers also confuses the situation as retailers in the inland provinces can suffer as people head for the coast to spend Christmas in resort towns.
